Paper_Metadata.Paper_Title: The crack formation, propagation and healing mechanisms of plasma sprayed multi-layer thermal/environmental barrier coatings during heat treatment

Raw_Evidence_Span: Si/Yb₂Si₂O₇-Yb₂SiO₅/Yb₂SiO₅/LaMgAl₁₁O₁₉ thermal and environmental barrier coatings (TEBCs) were fabricated on the SiC₆/SiC using atmospheric plasma spraying.
The thickness of Si, YbDS-YbMS, YbMS and LMA coating is about 100 μm, 50 μm, 50 μm and 100 μm, respectively.

Phase_Composition.Note: YbMS/YbDS phase ratio about 0.17 estimated from XRD peak intensity ratio; feedstock 32-125 μm
Self-synthesized feedstock, 32-125 μm; as-sprayed powder contained La₂O₃ phase

Composition.Note: Multi-layer coating architecture; composition derived from feedstock powder specifications. Substrate: SiCf/SiC ceramic composite.

Process_Text.original: Multi-layer Si/YbDS-YbMS/YbMS/LMA TEBCs was prepared on the surface of the SiCf/SiC by the method of atmospheric plasma spraying using the Multicoat Plasma Spray Unit (F4 gun, Multicoat, Oerlikon Metco, Switzerland). Before coating deposition, all SiCf/SiC substrates were sandblasted using 150 mesh corundum grits at 0.4 MPa for 30 s to remove SiC sealing layer and increase the surface roughness. Subsequently, the SiCf/SiC substrate was ultrasonically cleaned by deionized water and alcohol, and dried at 110 °C.
Process_Text.simplified: APS-deposited Si/Yb₂Si₂O₇-Yb₂SiO₅/Yb₂SiO₅/LaMgAl₁₁O₁₉ TEBC on SiCf/SiC using Multicoat F4 plasma gun. Substrate prep: sandblasted with 150 mesh corundum at 0.4 MPa for 30 s, ultrasonic cleaned, dried at 110 °C.

Key_Params.Substrate_Preparation: Sandblasted with 150 mesh corundum grits at 0.4 MPa for 30 s, ultrasonically cleaned, dried at 110 °C

Processing.Note: As-deposited state, no heat treatment applied to this item. Powder sizes: Si 30-60 μm (Shanghai ST-NANO); YbDS-YbMS 32-125 μm (Beijing Sunspraying); YbMS 32-125 μm (Beijing Sunspraying); LMA 32-125 μm (self-synthesized).

Structure_Text.original: Two kinds of microcracks including vertical crack (crack I) and horizontal crack (crack II) can be observed at YbDS-YbMS, YbMS and LMA coating after deposition. The shrinkage solidification of splat and CTE mismatch of coating between substrate would produce residual stress during coating deposition, which formed microcracks in the coating to release stress. The Si bond coat provided excellent bonding strength between EBCs system and SiCf/SiC, and no evident microcracks in ceramic coating were observed at the Si bond coat. The CTE of Si is lower than that of SiCf/SiC, indicating the compressive stress was formed at the Si bond coat and effectively restrain the crack formation. The quenching stress of as-deposited Si, YbDS, YbMS, and LMA coating prepared on SiCf/SiC surface is about 0.26 GPa, 0.35 GPa, 0.89 GPa, 1.11 GPa, respectively.
Structure_Text.simplified: As-deposited ceramic layers (YbDS-YbMS, YbMS, LMA) contained vertical and horizontal microcracks from quenching stress and CTE mismatch. Si bond coat was crack-free due to compressive stress. Quenching stresses: Si 0.26, YbDS 0.35, YbMS 0.89, LMA 1.11 GPa.

Structure_Text.original: Vertical crack was formed in the heat-treated LMA coating due to crystallization of amorphous phase and release of residual stress. The vertical crack was deflected at YbMS-LMA interface, and bridged with crack in the YbMS layer. The vertical crack did not connect with crack in the YbDS-YbMS layer. The bifurcation of cracks can be observed at the heat-treated YbDS-YbMS layer. A good interfacial bonding still can be observed at interface between Si layer and SiCf/SiC substrate. The crack width of LMA layer increased from 0.44 μm to 2.01 μm. The porosity of LMA layer increased to 13.7%. The porosity of YbMS layer decreased to 5.4% from 6.3% (spray conditions). Mud cracks with different modes were formed at YbDS-YbMS layer.
Structure_Text.simplified: After 950 °C heat treatment: LMA layer showed vertical cracks from crystallization shrinkage, porosity increased to 13.7%, crack width to 2.01 μm. YbMS layer porosity decreased to 5.4% via viscous flow. YbDS-YbMS layer showed mud cracks and bifurcation. Cracks in LMA bridged into YbMS but terminated at YbDS-YbMS. Si bond coat maintained good bonding.

Porosity.Note: LMA layer porosity; increased from 10.2% as-deposited due to crystallization-induced shrinkage and channel crack formation. YbMS layer porosity decreased to 5.4%.

Structure_Text.original: The vertical crack formed at 950 °C would continue to propagate into YbDS-YbMS layer with the heat-treated temperature up to 1050 °C. Many vertical cracks were formed at YbDS-YbMS layer after heat treatment at 1050 °C rather than horizontal cracks. Crack spheroidization was observed at YbDS-YbMS coating. The LMA layer porosity decreased to 8.2% and crack width decreased to 1.29 μm attributed to viscous flow. LaAlO₃ phase was detected at LMA coating.
Structure_Text.simplified: At 1050 °C: vertical cracks propagated further into YbDS-YbMS layer; many vertical cracks formed in YbDS-YbMS. LMA porosity decreased to 8.2%, crack width to 1.29 μm via viscous flow. Crack spheroidization in YbDS-YbMS. LaAlO₃ appeared in LMA layer.

Structure_Text.original: The cracks were firstly formed in the LMA coating due to the lower crystallization temperature and higher CTE, and continued to propagate into YbMS layer form bridging crack. The penetrated crack in the coating cannot heal due to the large crack width prevent sintering. Many pores still existed in the YbDS-YbMS layer due to the lacking of driving force of sintering. A good interfacial bonding still can be observed at interface between Si layer and SiC/SiC substrate. The ratio of crack width to porosity of LMA, YbDS-YbMS and YbMS layer is about 0.33, 0.63 and 0.21, respectively.
Structure_Text.simplified: At 1200 °C: cracks propagated from LMA into YbMS via bridging. Penetrated cracks could not heal. YbDS-YbMS retained pores from insufficient sintering. Crack width to porosity ratios: LMA 0.33, YbDS-YbMS 0.63, YbMS 0.21. Si bond coat still well bonded. M→T phase transformation accompanied by 9.24% and 5.01 vol% expansion for YbDS and YbMS respectively.

Structure_Text.original: The vertical crack penetrated through ceramic coating. The formation and growth of the vertical crack mainly caused by the crack bridging in every layer rather than completely caused by the excessive thermal stress. Horizontal cracks can be observed at the interface between YbMS region and YbDS region in YbDS-YbMS layer. The Si layer showed compressive stress (~136 MPa) and vertical cracks terminated at the Si surface. Al₂O₃ and LaAlO₃ phases disappeared and La₂O₃ second phase appeared in LMA coating.
Structure_Text.simplified: At 1300 °C: vertical cracks penetrated through entire ceramic coating via bridging mechanism. Horizontal cracks at YbMS-YbDS interfaces in mixed layer. La₂O₃ appeared, Al₂O₃ and LaAlO₃ disappeared in LMA. Si bond coat still crack-free with compressive stress.

Structure_Text.original: The vertical crack was also formed at coating but the crack density did not increase with the increasing of temperature. Horizontal crack and bifurcated crack were also formed at YbMS layer and YbDS-YbMS layer. The vertical cracks provide fast diffusion path for oxygen into Si layer, thus the Si was subjected to slight oxidation. The micro-crack then was formed at the interface between Si layer and YbDS-YbMS layer due to the oxidation of Si. Spallation crack was occurred at Si surface.
Structure_Text.simplified: At 1350 °C: vertical crack density did not increase vs 1300 °C. Si bond coat showed slight oxidation, causing interfacial micro-cracks between Si and YbDS-YbMS. Spallation crack appeared at Si surface. Horizontal and bifurcated cracks in YbMS and YbDS-YbMS layers.

Structure.Note: LMA crack width 3.28 μm is the largest among all heat-treated conditions. Spallation crack at Si surface indicates onset of coating failure.
